items.title: Sinc
items.description: Full-stack finance app for couples: splits expenses, tracks cards, installments, fixed costs and goals, and shows who owes whom. With AI (Gemini), typing "lunch 25 pix" fills in the entry, and expenses can be logged via WhatsApp.
items.challenge: Managing money as a couple means knowing, for every expense, who paid, how to split it and how much each one owes the other. Spreadsheets could not keep up with that routine.
items.solution: A Node.js/Express API with MongoDB and a Vue 3 front end that bring together transactions, cards, installments, goals and fixed expenses, with a balance dashboard for the couple and natural-language entry via Gemini.
decisions: Supabase for authentication only: the API validates the token and keeps a mirror of the user in MongoDB, where all business data lives.
Per-couple isolation (household): every record is stored with its creator's household and queries only return that couple's data, so many couples can share the same database.
Expense splitting modelled in the domain (individual, 50/50 or custom), with backend validation that the partner belongs to the same couple.
Fixed expenses as recurring templates: launching the month creates a real transaction, keeping history faithful to what happened.
highlights: AI-powered entry (Gemini): typing "lunch 25 pix" fills in the form, just confirm it.
Expense logging by WhatsApp message, via the WhatsApp Cloud API.
Dashboard with income vs. expenses, spending by category and who owes whom.
Credit cards, open installments and savings goals with deposits and withdrawals.

items.title: My Finances
items.description: Full-stack app for personal financial management.
items.challenge: Excel spreadsheets were no longer sufficient for effective financial control and tracking personal goals.
items.solution: I developed a full-stack application with a NestJS/GraphQL backend and a Vue.js 3 frontend, creating interactive dashboards for visual management.
decisions: GraphQL API with NestJS and Apollo Server, consumed on the front end through Apollo Client.
JWT authentication with Passport.js and an e-mail password reset flow using Nodemailer.
Automated backend routines: generating fixed-expense transactions, closing card statements and reminding about upcoming bills.
highlights: Dashboard with reactive charts and filters by period, category and description.
Credit cards with monthly statements generated and closed automatically.
Savings goals and CSV export of filtered transactions.

items.title: Portfolio
items.description: This dynamic portfolio, built with Vue 3, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS, employs Glassmorphism principle.
items.challenge: Build a portfolio that reflects my taste in design (glassmorphism, dark mode and Apple's aesthetic) without giving up performance, especially on phones.
items.solution: A Vue 3, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS app with PT/EN, case study pages, a keyboard-driven search (⌘K) and glass effects that adapt to the device.
decisions: Adaptive glass: backdrop-filter on desktop only. On phones the cards use a more opaque tint, because blurring behind every card while scrolling stalled rendering.
Background blobs built with radial gradients instead of filter: blur, with the same look at a fraction of the GPU cost.
WebP images (from ~550 KB to ~70 KB) and brand icons inlined as SVG, with no extra runtime dependency.
All content lives in the translation files: adding a project or a language never touches a component.
highlights: Command palette (⌘K / Ctrl K) to navigate, switch theme and language or copy the e-mail.
Technology dock that filters projects by stack.
Current section and reading progress indicator at the top of the page.

items.title: Beauty Manager
items.description: Academic application for beauty salon scheduling. The project also included low, medium, and high-fidelity prototypes and an adapted Design System.
items.challenge: My mother's beauty salon struggled with manual scheduling, which caused errors like double bookings or forgotten appointments.
items.solution: I created a scheduling application with a REST API (Python/FastAPI) and a React frontend, allowing clients and administrators to manage schedules.
decisions: REST API in Python/FastAPI separate from the React front end, with ADMIN and CLIENT roles and distinct permissions: admins manage services and professionals, clients book and cancel appointments.
highlights: Built as a pair for the Integrated Project I course at UFC, with 100% of the requirements implemented.
Full UX process: low, mid and high-fidelity prototypes and an adapted Design System.
